stem: A team wants AWS Compute Optimizer's own rightsizing findings for two different resources: an EC2 Auto Scaling group whose instance type might already be wrong, and a Lambda function whose memory setting might already be wrong. Which TWO statements about Compute Optimizer are correct? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Compute Optimizer requires enhanced infrastructure metrics enabled before it can analyze anything
Compute Optimizer analyzes the Lambda function's duration and memory-utilization history and recommends a specific memory value
A mixed instances policy automatically rightsizes the ASG's instance type
Compute Optimizer analyzes the ASG's history and flags it as under- or over-provisioned
Lambda SnapStart automatically adjusts the function's memory setting

rationale: Compute Optimizer analyzes a Lambda function's actual CloudWatch duration and memory-utilization history and can recommend a specific memory value, directly answering whether the current setting is already right. It likewise analyzes an EC2 Auto Scaling group's history and reports it as under-provisioned, over-provisioned, or already optimal. Enhanced infrastructure metrics is an optional paid feature that extends the lookback window to 93 days; Compute Optimizer analyzes up to 14 days of history by default without it, so it is not a requirement to get any analysis at all. A mixed instances policy only changes which instance types and purchase options an Auto Scaling group can launch; it does not analyze utilization or automatically pick a rightsized type. Lambda SnapStart snapshots and resumes an already-initialized execution environment to cut cold starts; it does not analyze or adjust the function's memory setting.
